actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

actions.description: Set the seed used by the simulated world's random number generators for subsequent steps, without resetting the world. The accepted seed is echoed in the receipt.

facts.text: RoboDojo is an eval-only release that provides the simulator client, benchmark tasks, asset and config validation and result artifacts, and it lists 42 simulation tasks
TaskEnv extends BaseEnv and composes the robot, scene, camera and capture managers
BaseEnv launches the simulator with gym.make('IsaacRLEnv-V0', ...)
IsaacRLEnv-V0 is registered with entry point env.environment.isaac.isaac_rl_env:IsaacRLEnv
The simulation timestep is dt 0.004 s with decimation 1
The common task configuration selects the dual_x5 robot
The dual_x5 embodiment has two six-joint arms and one end-effector dimension per arm
With two target arms the observation and action names are left_arm, left_ee, right_arm and right_ee
The eval client assigns the policy's arm_joint_state values directly as the joint position target
The robot, object, material and layout assets are downloaded separately under Assets/
The policy gripper command is clipped to 0 to 1 before it is mapped to the gripper scale
ObsManager publishes each target arm's joint state and each gripper's normalized state
TaskEnv.reset reloads the scene, resets the robot, advances 300 render-disabled steps and resets the cameras
TaskEnv.step forwards a ControlSeq list to RobotManager.control_robot
The control queue holds MetaControl entries and pops one per environment step
Each task sets its own step limit; stack_blocks uses 550
Seed updates call seed_everywhere with the global seed
The X5 initial joint positions are 0 for joints 1 to 6 and 0.044 for the gripper joints

determinism.notes: reset(seed) or cap.world.seed.v1 fixes the fake's initial joint offsets and its dynamics are deterministic, so the fake repeats a trajectory for the same seed and actions; upstream seeds the scene layouts and Isaac Sim physics, so a seed does not give the same trajectory on the two

gaps: the fake is an analytic joint-space stand-in: no Isaac Sim, no rigid-body dynamics, contacts, friction, deformable objects, actuators, sensors or domain randomization

the 42 task scenes and their task-specific rewards and success checks are not modelled; the fake exposes only the common dual-X5 joint command and state convention, returns a placeholder reward and never terminates or truncates

upstream TaskEnv.step takes a list of ControlSeq/MetaControl objects built by the eval client; the Gymnasium bridge passes the policy action dict straight to the fake, so the fake interprets that dict as joint positions instead of queueing control sequences
the fake observation is the 14-number joint/gripper state vector; the upstream observation is a dict with vision, state, action and instruction, and the camera RGB/depth arrays are not modelled
the arm joint position limits live in the downloaded USD asset, which is not in the clone; the fake leaves the arm command unbounded and bounds only the normalized gripper command to 0 to 1
the fake was not compared with the upstream environment (Isaac Sim, Isaac Lab and the assets were not available where the gate ran), and no snapshot or restore is offered

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
